title: Plugins & Integrations
intro: Bring application commands, Python extensions and service entries together. Enable on demand with the existing project protections.
search: Search plugin name, description or ID
notVerified: Publisher and source are self-declared and have not been reviewed. Inspect the contents first.
nonSensitiveConfig: Non-sensitive options only. Configure API keys and credentials in the existing AI settings.
resourceHelp: Download for use in the existing import interface
uninstallHelp: Stop pending operations and remove the plugin from the list. Keep the original package for re-import; manuscripts are unaffected.
emptyHelp: Import a local package or download a working example. Installation and enabling never start scripts.
integrationsHelp: These are configuration entries, not connection checks. Opening this page does not connect every model or start external programs.
existingIntegration: Uses existing settings, credentials and permissions. Check connection status in the corresponding feature.
developerHelp: Version 1 supports declarative actions, isolated Python and existing application entries, with stable IDs, versions and file hashes.
stepManifest: Create manifest.json with identity, version, author, minimum app version and action permissions.
stepContributions: Declare commands, non-sensitive settings, Python scripts or downloadable resources.
stepZip: Place the manifest and listed UTF-8 files at the ZIP root, with SHA-256 hashes, then preview the import.
stepRun: Enable explicitly after installation. Review the plan; sensitive operations still require author approval.
boundary: Code runs only in the existing WASI sandbox. It can call declared Actions within current project, persona and context permissions. No install hooks, host files, arbitrary network, shell, SQL or credential access.
future: VS Code and Obsidian plugins are not directly compatible. No automatic npm or pip installs. Native protocol adapters need separate development and review; AI and image services use existing settings.
installNotice: New and updated plugins start disabled without code execution. Enabling does not grant every Action; permissions are checked at execution.
updateNotice: This updates an installed plugin. Old package files remain; the update starts disabled and settings need review.
runNotice: Run this fixed plan in the existing Python Control panel. Results, stop and approval controls appear there. No automatic manuscript or Canon commits.
openProject: Open a novel before running this command.
localFirst: Local packages · On-demand execution · Project protections
disabledHelp: Enable this plugin to run commands. Enabling does not execute scripts.
noMatchHelp: Try a plugin name, purpose or ID, or clear the search to see all plugins.
nowEnabled: Plugin enabled. No commands have been executed.
nowDisabled: Plugin disabled. Unfinished operations have been revoked.
uninstalled: Plugin removed from the list. Its original package is retained.
serviceHelp_ai: Manage API providers, credentials and models using the existing secure storage.
serviceHelp_models: Assign models to writing tasks and configure supported parameters and context budgets.
serviceHelp_codex: Reuse the current Codex login and controlled tools for on-demand application tasks.
serviceHelp_images: Connect your local ComfyUI. Opening settings does not start an external program.
serviceHelp_python: Compose authorized application actions in isolated Python and inspect real receipts.
serviceHelp_world: Import experiment templates and test explicit rules with the existing solvers.
serviceHelp_skills: Read the usage, installation requirements and boundaries of writing Skills.
invalidValue: Enter a valid number for “{{name}}”. Integer options cannot contain decimals.
